description: A half-open range of hours follows the closing hour of a shop
code:
open = 9
close = 13
hours = open..<close
assert(hours, [9, 10, 11, 12])
close = 15
hours

description: A closed range lists every floor from the basement to the top floor
code:
lowest = -1
highest = 3
floors = lowest..=highest
assert(floors, [-1, 0, 1, 2, 3])
highest = 5
[floors.length, floors.at(-1)]

description: A membership test against a closed range accepts whole star ratings only
code:
stars = 4
valid = stars in 1..=5
assert(valid, true)
stars = 4.5
assert(valid, false)
stars = 6
valid

description: Mapping a range of positions lists the coordinates of a grid that grows
code:
width = 2
height = 2
cells = (0..<width * height).map(i -> [i % width, Math.floor(i / width)])
assert(cells, [[0, 0], [1, 0], [0, 1], [1, 1]])
width = 3
cells.at(-1)

description: A class-level range rule gives every shift its hours and follows each shift's end
code:
class Shift(start, end):
    this.start = start
    this.end = end
morning = Shift(8, 12)
$Shift.hours = $Shift.start..<$Shift.end
evening = Shift(18, 20)
assert(evening.hours, [18, 19])
morning.end = 10
morning.hours

description: A range empties when its bounds cross and fills again when they part
code:
first = 5
last = 3
span = first..=last
assert(span, [])
last = 7
span.length

description: A comprehension reads a range as its source
code:
top = 4
squares = [i * i for i in 1..=top]
assert(squares, [1, 4, 9, 16])
top = 5
squares.sum()

description: A fractional bound raises a TypeError and leaves the previous list in place
code:
count = 3
items = 0..<count
failure = ""
try:
    count = 2.5
catch error:
    failure = error
assert(failure, TypeError("Range bounds must be integers"))
[count, items]

description: A range of more than 100,000 items raises before any item is built
code:
size = 10
slots = 0..<size
failure = ""
try:
    size = 200000
catch error:
    failure = error
assert(failure, TypeError("Range is too large"))
[size, slots.length]

description: A range of positions pairs every name with its index even when names repeat
code:
names = ["ann", "bob", "ann"]
pairs = (0..<names.length).map(i -> [i, names[i]])
assert(pairs, [[0, "ann"], [1, "bob"], [2, "ann"]])
names = ["cy"]
pairs

description: An undefined bound makes the range null until the bound is set
code:
settings = {}
levels = 1..=settings.top
assert(levels, null)
settings.top = 3
levels

description: An explanation quotes a range as it is written
code:
first = 1
last = 3
span = first..<last
assert(span, [1, 2])
(why span).map(step -> step.rule)
